newsitem.title: MEXICO: Telmex Q1 net profit falls.
newsitem.headline: Telmex Q1 net profit falls.

text.p: Mexican telephone company Telefonos de Mexico SA (Telmex) reported first quarter earnings of 3.207 billion pesos versus 4.333 billion pesos during the same quarter of 1996.
Earnings per share were 0.38 pesos versus 0.47 pesos during the year-ago quarter.
Telmex's consolidated revenues during the quarter were 12.99 billion pesos, down 0.9 percent on the 13.10 billion pesos during the same period of the year before.
Telmex's operating profits during the quarter grew, however, to 4.9 billion pesos from 4.645 billion during the same three months of 1996.
International long-distance minutes grew 8.5 percent during the quarter, but international long-distance revenues fell 20.8 percent to 2.936 billion pesos compared to the same quarter of 1996.
Domestic long-distance minutes rose 3.9 percent but revenues fell 4.9 percent to 3.641 billion pesos during the quarter.
Local service generated 5.836 billion pesos during the quarter, a rise of 16 percent compared to the year-ago quarter. The company's integral financial gain during the quarter
was 398 million pesos versus a gain of 1.697 billion pesos during the year-ago quarter.
Telmex said in a statement its long-distance revenues had fallen because of the start of competition in the Mexican market.
"Although the effect of competition was weak during the quarter, we expect this effect to increase as we lose market share," the company said.
Telmex said it had 8,881,343 telephone lines in service at the end of the quarter, an increase of 0.4 percent compared to the same quarter of 1996.
The firm's operating costs not including depreciation and amortization were 4.992 billion pesos during the quarter, down 3.2 percent compared to the same period of last year.

In the cellular telephone unit, quarterly operating profits fell to 43 million pesos from 56 million pesos in the year-ago quarter. Telmex said it signed up 105,676 new cellular telephone customers during the quarter.
The company added that during the quarter, it repurchased 364 million shares as part of a buy-back program. The total number of outstanding shares at quarter's end was 8,510,484,006, it said.
